reason: I'll strengthen the bones first; the picture shows spaces for mineral and says it resists compression.
expectation: I expect the mineral to fill the spaces and make the bone framework harder, though I'm not sure exactly how.

alternatives.reason: The front attachments also clearly need muscle cells, but I'll start with the bones.

effect: The bones are strengthened while the joint remains able to move, so I'll build a muscle next.
reaction: The contrast between hard bone and the still-movable joint is helpful.
reason: The front attachments have a space for muscle cells, matching the goal of building muscles around the elbow.
expectation: I expect a muscle to form between the front tendons; I'm not sure yet how the game will show it moving the joint.

alternatives.reason: The back attachments also need muscle, but I'll start with the front.

effect: The front cells formed a biceps that pulls to bend the elbow; the back attachments still need muscle.
reaction: Seeing the pull connected to bending makes the attachment's purpose clearer.
reason: I'll use the only available combination to build muscle at the back attachments.
expectation: I expect a back muscle to form and pull the forearm in the opposite direction, though I'm not sure how it will be shown.

effect: The triceps result completes the arm and shows that attachment position, rather than a different kind of muscle cell, changes the direction of movement.
reaction: The contrast with the biceps made the two pulls easy to understand.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the biceps and triceps was most worthwhile: the arrows connected their positions to bending and straightening the elbow.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding mineral was the least engaging action, although the result usefully explained hardness and the movable joint.

surprise.text: The same kind of muscle cell can produce opposite movements depending on where the muscle attaches.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary: the pictures showed spaces for mineral and muscle cells, though the compatible pairings were offered rather than discovered.

continue.text: Yes, I would try another chapter: seeing how the parts fit together and affect movement made me curious about other body systems.
